items.title: Marty Napoleon interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York, New York, January 16, 1999
items.q: the bass players fluctuated, either Arvell Shaw or Benny Moten, different bass players. But with Charlie Shavers and Coleman Hawkins.

ctx.x: Yeah the first place was Sweden, and we got into this town and the place was closed. There wasn’t a thing in town. I met a guy and he could speak English and he spoke to me, “you with Louis Armstrong?” I says, “hey where is everybody?” He says, “what do you mean?” “I don’t see anybody in the streets, nobody walking, the shops are closing.” He says, “Louis Armstrong’s here.” I said, “what do you mean?” He said, “they closed the whole town,” they were getting prepared to go see Louis at the concert. I swear to God,…

get back on the bus. And we just had time to put your bags down, wash your face, shave, and run downstairs. So I went past the dining room, and Arvell Shaw was sitting in the dining room. And I said how are we going to eat? He says, “man I’ve got to get something, I’m starving, I’m just having some soup.” I said, “I’m going to do that too.” So I sat down with him and I ordered some soup.
